text:
An approval screen can answer the wrong question.

CERT-In reports an AI-assisted campaign targeting Indian financial entities through their payment interfaces. Its earlier advisory describes stolen credentials enabling direct payment calls that bypass application checks.

That distinction is what I think leaders should examine: a screen can show that someone approved a payment without establishing that the transfer actually depends on that approval.

The business question is whether permission survives the journey from decision to money moving. If the final transfer accepts a different basis for permission, reviewing the screen leaves the crucial dependency untested.

I would ask business and IT owners to trace one approved payment together. Follow the amount, recipient and approval through to the transfer, then identify what would stop it if those details changed or the approval were missing.

One trace cannot establish that every payment is protected. But it can turn a reassuring demonstration into a concrete examination of what the system requires before money leaves.
